A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and research questions. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B report original policy-compression experiments, latent-manifold analyses, and fine-tuning comparisons in Mountain Car and Reacher.

after.justification: The original empirical studies remain, with additional compression experiments in Hopper and HalfCheetah and a policy-representation analysis.

M1.justification: The novelty-filtered policy dataset, autoencoder with behavioral reconstruction loss, frozen decoder, and latent-space policy optimization remain unchanged. Newly specified activation functions and evaluation details do not establish an algorithmic or architectural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds compression evaluation in Hopper and HalfCheetah. Hopper introduces forward, backward, standstill, and jump tasks; HalfCheetah introduces forward, backward, frontflip, and backflip tasks. This substantially extends the represented dynamics and behaviors beyond Mountain Car and Reacher; fine-tuning coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The existing PPO, DDPG, TD3, SAC, and Parameter PGPE comparisons are retained. Figures 4–5 newly include a Best in Dataset policy-performance reference alongside the learning algorithms, adding a comparator within those reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix B replaces the stated 5D/8D latent-space grids with 10,000 random samples for dimensions above three and changes Reacher's reported PGPE center learning rate from 0.01 to 0.1. New Hopper/HalfCheetah experiments use 10k-policy datasets and 5D/8D/16D representations. These reported settings do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds the Policy Representation Range analysis and Figure 6, comparing reward distributions from randomly sampled Small and Large Mountain Car policies. This directly examines whether larger networks represent richer behaviors. Existing baseline-size ablations and appendix manifold visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly documents interpolation and terminal-value extension when aggregating PGPE runs, plus 10-episode intermediate and 100-episode final evaluations. New compression results report 10-seed confidence intervals, and the representation-range analysis reports five-seed intervals. Existing reported run counts remain unchanged; an increase in repetitions of retained experiments is not established.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Hopper/HalfCheetah recovery results, including HalfCheetah forward recovery of 1.84 with 95% CI [1.41, 2.39] at 16D. Figure 6 adds reward-distribution findings, including broader height-task coverage for Large policies. Mountain Car recovery values in Table 1 and v1 Table 2/v2 Table 3 are unchanged; the additions are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2 adds the missing 1/(T+1) normalization to the state-occupancy distribution and distinguishes continuous probability measures from finite probability simplices. Appendix B corrects the latent-policy trajectory probability factorization. These are limited mathematical corrections; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: unsupervised behavioral compression, dimensionality governed primarily by environment complexity, compression up to five orders of magnitude, and efficient latent-space fine-tuning. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 adds interpretation of beyond-dataset generalization, task-dependent recovery, and variance obscuring Hopper's dimensionality trend. Appendix B connects the new representation-range findings to network expressivity while explicitly limiting that evidence to random weight sampling in one environment. Existing dataset-coverage and fine-tuning limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code link alongside the supplementary-material reference, specifies autoencoder ELU activation placement, and explains PGPE evaluation and curve aggregation. Appendix B also supplies the new environments' reward conditions, state bounds, horizons, and configuration details. Much of the original implementation documentation is retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds substantial positioning within Weight Space Learning, discussing goal-conditioned generators, checkpoint models, hyper-representations, parameter symmetries, and policy fingerprinting. It explains how behavioral reconstruction differs from these approaches. Additional expressivity references support the new analysis, extending the original positioning beyond policy manifolds, quality diversity, and policy optimization.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, rewrites selected explanatory passages, adds an ethics statement, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. The main section sequence and narrative remain recognizable; new scientific content does not amount to a wholesale structural rewrite.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 are substantially enlarged and reorganized from four-panel rows into 2-by-2 grids, with revised colors, legends, and dataset-reference lines. Table 1 gains bolding and shading; a new recovery table and reward-distribution figure are added. The appendix manifold plots are retained, resized, and relocated rather than replaced with new results.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for behavioral compression beyond v1's two environments. Hopper/HalfCheetah results with ten-seed confidence intervals support recovery beyond the training dataset on several tasks, addressing v1's tentative attribution of such recovery to generalization or evaluation variance. The new diagnostic, clearer implementation reporting, and expanded research positioning improve assessability. Fine-tuning evidence still covers only Mountain Car and Reacher, so the broader validation principally strengthens the compression contribution.
